# Scanning Reality: Small Pool-Supplies Retailer, Garage Stock (Malta)

**TLDR:** Most of the stock (branded chemical buckets, Intex/Bestway pools, test kits, pumps, robotic cleaners) arrives with a factory EAN-13 and will scan; the reliable *non*-scannable pockets are repackaged/decanted chemicals, loose spare parts, unboxed floats, and anything sold by measure — these need retailer-assigned internal codes (GS1 reserves prefixes 02/20–29 exactly for this). Physical scan pain comes from curved 5–25 kg buckets, shrink-wrap glare, sun/chlorine-faded labels, and multipack inner-vs-outer-carton EAN confusion. Chlorine vapour in a closed garage demonstrably corrodes metal and electronics ("destroyed pumps, controllers... electronics" per pool-industry storage guidance), so the counting tablet/scanner must NOT live in the chemical garage. Malta's pool season peaks mid-June–mid-September (swimming viable May–October), so full stock-take belongs in November–February, with a delivery-verification pass in March–April.

## 1) Typical product mix

Grounded in actual Malta retailers (Bubble Hub MT, Splash Store Malta, The Model Shop Malta) plus generic pool-trade catalogs (PoolSupplies.com, Inyo Pools):

| Category | Typical form in a small Malta shop | EUR price anchors (Malta unless noted) |
|---|---|---|
| Chlorine tablets/granules | 1 kg jars up to 5 kg buckets (20 g and 200 g tabs); 25 kg drums on trade side | Multifunction 200 g tabs 5 kg €58.95; Bromo-Cloro 20 g tabs 5 kg €109.95 (bubblehub.mt); 5-in-1 multitabs sold in 5 kg buckets ≈250 tabs (Splash Store Malta); used-market 5 kg €45 (FB Marketplace, Mosta) |
| Liquid chemicals | 1 L bottles and 5 L "trade size" jerrycans (clarifier, oil/grease remover, phosphate remover, liquid chlorine, acid) | Clarifier 1 L €21.95; Oil Out 5 L €74.95; Phos Out 5 L €84.95 (bubblehub.mt) |
| pH correctors | pH− granules / pH+ powder in 5 kg tubs | pH− 5 kg €31.50; pH+ 5 kg €28.95 (bubblehub.mt) |
| Algaecide / problem treatments | 1–5 L bottles, flocculant cubes/gel packs | Jolly Gel floc 4-pack €17.95 (bubblehub.mt) |
| Test kits/strips | Test strips tubs, liquid/drop kits, digital testers, reagent refills | dedicated Water Testing category at bubblehub.mt (strips/digital/liquid/reagents) |
| Pumps & filters | Cartridge + sand filter systems, filter cartridges, sand/glass media bags (media often 20–25 kg sacks) | Filters & Cartridges category (bubblehub.mt); pumps/filter pumps stocked by The Model Shop Malta |
| Hoses/fittings & spare parts | "Pool Parts" / "Hot Tub Parts" bins — O-rings, adaptors, hose clips, valves, often loose | bubblehub.mt Pool Parts / Hot Tub Parts categories |
| Inflatable pools, kids pools & floats | Boxed Intex/Bestway; floats as lilos/rings, air beds, inflatable furniture — display units often unboxed | bubblehub.mt Floats & Inflatables + Inflatable/Kids Pools categories |
| Frame pools | Large heavy cartons (oversized boxes) | bubblehub.mt Frame Pools category |
| Covers, ladders, cleaning kits, skimmers | Covers rolled/bagged, ladders semi-assembled, cleaning kits carded | The Model Shop Malta (covers, cleaning kits, skimmers) |
| Robotic cleaners | Branded boxed units (Dolphin/Zodiac class) — standard trade items | generic trade catalogs (Inyo Pools) — Malta price unknown |
| Hot tubs & accessories | Common sideline in Malta (Intex/Lay-Z-Spa) | bubblehub.mt Hot Tubs categories |

## 2) Barcode presence per category

GS1 baseline: any branded product traded at retail carries a GTIN encoded in an EAN/UPC barcode (GS1 US), and **each packaging configuration — unit, multipack, case, pallet — gets its own GTIN** (GS1 Canada). For goods with no manufacturer code, GS1 reserves **Restricted Circulation Numbers (prefixes 02 and 20–29)** so the retailer assigns internal in-store barcodes, historically for variable-measure items (GS1 prefix summary; GS1 South Africa glossary defines the Variable Measure Number for POS scanning of such products).

**Normally HAS a factory EAN/GTIN:**
- Branded chemical buckets/jars/bottles (Steinbach, Melpool, Intex, Bayrol-class products) — printed on the wrap-around label
- Test strip tubs, drop kits, digital testers
- Boxed pumps, filter systems, filter cartridges (blister/boxed)
- Inflatable pools, frame pools, floats **in their retail box/sleeve**
- Covers, ladders, robotic cleaners (boxed)

**Typically does NOT have a scannable manufacturer EAN (needs internal codes/labels):**
- Bulk/repackaged chemicals: tablets or granules decanted from a 25 kg trade drum into unbranded tubs or sold by weight — the drum's code identifies the drum, not the portion sold (variable-measure case → GS1 RCN territory)
- Loose spare parts: O-rings, fittings, hose clips sold individually from an inner carton — the barcode is on the carton, not the piece
- Unboxed floats/lilos on display or sold after the sleeve is discarded — code was on the discarded packaging
- Anything sold by measure (hose by the metre, filter media scooped/split from sacks)
- Generic/import white-label items from non-GS1 suppliers — may carry no code or a duplicate/invalid one

**Problem surfaces for scanners (even where an EAN exists):**
- **Curved buckets/bottles:** curved surfaces such as bottles or tubes distort bars and reduce readability (iDPRT troubleshooting guide); glossy labels, metal parts and curved surfaces create glare (Tera Digital)
- **Shrink-wrap/plastic glare:** reflective surfaces that create glare, "such as a package wrapped in plastic," are a named environmental scan-failure factor (Scandit)
- **Faded/damaged labels:** smudging or fading, insufficient contrast, torn/crinkled/obscured codes are among the most common quality failures (Scandit; Finale Inventory) — directly relevant to sun-bleached Maltese garage stock and chemically-attacked chlorine-bucket labels
- **Poor lighting/dirt in garages:** insufficient or uneven lighting and dirt/dust/smudges on label or lens degrade scans (Scandit)
- **Multipacks, inner vs outer carton:** since each packaging level carries a *different* GTIN (GS1 Canada), scanning an outer carton EAN when selling units (or vice versa) miscounts; multiple barcodes in the scanner's field of view also cause wrong-code reads (Scandit)
- **Oversized boxes (frame pools):** barcode may be on one face of a 1.5 m carton stacked label-inward; physical access, not decoding, is the failure mode (inference from stock handling, not a cited source)

**Practical implication:** plan the inventory system for a hybrid — scan-first for boxed branded goods, plus a printed internal-barcode/QR label regime (GS1 RCN-style 20–29 prefixes or plain internal QRs) for repackaged chemicals, loose parts and unboxed floats.

## 3) Environment hazard: chlorine vapour vs electronics

Two independent pool-industry sources support the corrosion claim:

- **Chloramine Consulting (natatorium engineering consultancy):** chlorine must be stored separately from "any other types of chlorine, any type of acid, **metal equipment and electronics**"; "Both acid and chlorine have fumes that will destroy steel"; commercial pump rooms are routinely "corroded beyond repair" from bad ventilation/storage, with "destroyed pumps, **controllers**, filters, valves, bolts" observed; "Good ventilation is essential to help prevent rust/corrosion and vapor interactions."
- **HASA (US pool-chemical manufacturer, Jan 2026, author is a PHTA CPO instructor):** "Poor storage can lead to leaks, corrosion, or dangerous chemical reactions"; "Both chlorine and acid can corrode metal and concrete over time"; chemicals should be kept "cool, dry, and ventilated," and **residential garages are explicitly called out as unsuitable** ("aren't ideal as they often lack ventilation and temperature control"); avoid storage "in areas connected to homes, offices, or pool equipment rooms."

**Concrete placement advice for the tablet/scanner:**
1. **Never store the device in the chemical garage.** It should live in the house/office/car and enter the garage only for the duration of a count. Trichlor buckets off-gas corrosive vapour continuously; a closed Maltese garage in summer heat concentrates it.
2. **Never charge it in the garage.** Charging contacts, USB ports and dock springs are the first things chlorine vapour eats; corroded connectors are the classic early failure.
3. Between sessions keep it in a **sealed case/zip bag with silica gel** if it must transit the space; wipe it down after use (chloride dust settles on surfaces).
4. **Air the garage 10–15 minutes before a counting session** — for the device and, more importantly, the person (vapour also irritates lungs — HASA hazard-classification guidance).
5. Keep all chlorine buckets **tightly lidded** and store chlorine away from acid (mixing vapours is a toxic-gas and corrosion multiplier — both sources).
6. If a fixed scanner/label printer is ever wanted at the stock location, put it in a **separate ventilated ante-room or cabinet**, not the chemical bay — mirroring the industry rule of separating chemical rooms from equipment rooms.
7. Budget consequence: assume **shortened electronics life for anything resident near stock**; a cheap rugged Android + spare beats one expensive tablet stored badly.

## 4) Seasonality and stock-take timing (Malta)

- Best hot-weather/pool period in Malta is **mid-June to mid-September** (WeatherSpark beach/pool score); locals swim comfortably **May through October**, with sea still ~20–25 °C in late October (Tripadvisor Malta forum; r/malta).
- Retail consequence: chemical and inflatable demand ramps **April–May** (pool openings, first heat), peaks June–August, tails through October. Winter (Nov–Feb) is the dead season with minimal turnover.
- **Stock-take timing advice:**
  - **Full annual count: November–January** — stock at its lowest, garage temperatures bearable, no sales pressure, chemical vapour load lowest (cooler = less off-gassing).
  - **Pre-season verification pass: March–April**, as container/pallet deliveries land — verify and internally label incoming stock (especially unbarcoded categories) *before* the rush, so summer selling runs on clean data.
  - **Avoid June–August counts:** peak sales disruption, peak garage heat (hard on people and devices), fastest stock movement making counts stale immediately.
  - Perpetual mini-counts (cycle counting) of the top movers — 5 kg tablet buckets, pH correctors, test strips — monthly during the season, since these are also the categories most exposed to repackaging/label-decay drift.

## Method notes
- All web research via Firecrawl (6 searches, 4 scrapes); no fallback needed.
- Prices are EUR as listed by Malta retailers (bubblehub.mt, Splash Store Malta, FB Marketplace Malta); pool.shop (EU) €74.95 for Melpool 20 g 5 kg as a non-Malta reference.
- Barcode presence per category combines GS1 rules (sourced) with standard retail practice; the category-level "has EAN" claims are industry-norm inference anchored on the GS1 GTIN framework, while the "no EAN for repackaged/variable-measure/loose items" claim is directly supported by GS1's Restricted Circulation Number scheme.
- Robotic cleaner Malta pricing: unknown (not needed for scanning analysis).

**Status:** DONE
**Summary:** Built the four-part scanning-reality picture with Malta-grounded product mix/prices, GS1-sourced barcode presence/absence analysis, dual-sourced chlorine-corrosion hazard with placement advice, and seasonality-driven stock-take timing.

# Shopify retail tooling from Malta — verified findings (mid-2026)

## 1. Shopify Payments in Malta — HYPOTHESIS WRONG for online, RIGHT in spirit for retail
The current help.shopify.com supported-countries list (checked 2026-07-09) **includes Malta**, and a dedicated "Shopify Payments for Malta" help page exists: Malta merchants can activate Shopify Payments for ONLINE checkout (cards, accelerated checkouts, local payment methods, 3D Secure). BUT the separate "Setting up Shopify Payments for POS" page states only countries where Shopify Payments supports BOTH online and in-person processing can use it on POS — that list (AU, BE, CA, CZ, DK, FI, FR, DE, IE, IT, LU, NL, NZ, SG, ES, CH, UK, US) **excludes Malta**. Net: a Malta merchant can take Shopify Payments online, but CANNOT process card-present payments through Shopify at the till — no Shopify card readers, no Tap to Pay (Tap to Pay requires in-person Shopify Payments; its published country list also does not name Malta).

## 2. Official POS hardware — not sold/shipped to Malta
Shopify Hardware Stores exist for 16 storefronts (US, UK, IE, DE, FR, IT, ES, NL, BE, DK, FI, CA en/fr, AU, NZ, SG) — no Malta. Documented guidance for everyone else: check the supported-hardware model list and "purchase hardware from a verified third-party retailer of your choice." Implication for Malta: payments-agnostic peripherals (supported barcode scanners, receipt printers, cash drawers) can be bought third-party and will work with POS, but Shopify card readers are pointless even if imported because in-person Shopify Payments isn't supported in Malta — card acceptance must run on an external terminal.

## 3. POS Lite vs Pro pricing — hypothesis CONFIRMED
POS Lite is included with every paid Shopify plan at no extra cost (basic in-person selling). POS Pro is an add-on at **USD $89/month per POS location** (USD $79/month per location with annual billing; original currency USD — Shopify's local-currency billing for Malta unknown). Pro adds staff permissions/unlimited POS staff, exchanges, save/email cart, ship-to-home / pickup fulfilment options, inventory counting/transfers (Stocky-class features), daily sales reports, in-store analytics, 2-year hardware warranty, etc.

## 4. Recording cash and custom/external payments so inventory decrements
Two documented mechanisms, both first-party:
- **POS custom payment types**: Shopify admin > Point of Sale channel > Settings > POS app (POS editor) > Checkout > "Add custom payment type" — explicitly intended for "checks or third-party terminals". A custom type (e.g. named "Revolut" or "SumUp") completes a normal POS order: Shopify records order number, customer, line items, total incl. taxes, timestamps and the payment-type label; no Shopify fees; funds are NOT processed by Shopify (they settle via the external processor). Because it produces a regular POS order, stock at the retail location adjusts like any other sale. Cash is a built-in tender, activated by default, toggleable per device.
- **Draft orders + Mark as paid** (admin/back-office path): create a draft order, optionally reserve inventory (reserved units become "Unavailable"), then "Mark as paid" when payment was received outside Shopify — the draft converts to a regular order and inventory is decremented/finalized.

## 5. POS offline mode — NOT Pro-gated
Documented on help.shopify.com: POS needs internet only to sync with admin, send email receipts, and capture card payments. **Offline checkout — accepting cash and any configured custom/manual payment methods (checks, third-party terminals) with no internet — is "available to all Shopify POS users"**, i.e. included in POS Lite; a second, separate optional feature ("Offline payments") extends offline selling to card payments via Shopify's own readers and must be activated in admin (irrelevant in Malta since Shopify card-present isn't supported). Documented offline limits: new products can't be created/saved offline, some product/customer search functions are internet-dependent, email receipts and admin sync queue until reconnection. So a Malta shop can keep ringing up cash + "Revolut/SumUp" custom-tender sales during an outage; the sales sync when connectivity returns.

## 6. Shopify mobile admin app (Android) — camera barcode scanning
The Shopify admin app has a built-in inventory scanner: Products > Scan inventory > (optional location) > scan product barcodes with the device camera to count/adjust stock. The app can also populate a product's barcode field by scanning with the camera when adding/updating products. In the POS app, the global search bar has a barcode icon for camera-scan product lookup (adds to cart/search). Limitation: external hardware barcode scanners in the POS app only add items to checkout — they can't add products to inventory. The help pages document "the Shopify app" without an Android exclusion for the inventory scanner.

## 7. External card readers Malta merchants actually use
Since Shopify card-present is unavailable, Malta retailers pair Shopify POS with an external terminal recorded as a custom payment type — no automatic amount sync: staff key the total into the reader, take payment there, then close the Shopify sale under the custom tender (double-entry risk is the known trade-off; reconciliation happens in the processor's dashboard).
- **SumUp (Malta storefront, sumup.com/en-mt, checked 2026-07-09)**: Solo Lite €34, Solo €79, Terminal (built-in printer) €169. Malta per-transaction fee not confirmed on the scraped page (unknown).
- **Revolut Reader**: launched in Malta July 2024 at **€49** with **0.8% + €0.02** per in-person transaction (launch-time figures; current Malta business-site page for the reader returned 404, so today's price unknown — verify in the Revolut Business app).

## Bottom line for a Malta merchant
Shopify works from Malta as: any plan + free POS Lite + third-party peripherals + cash/custom-payment tenders (SumUp/Revolut readers at €34–€169) + Shopify Payments for the ONLINE store only. Offline cash/custom selling and camera-based inventory scanning are included free. What you cannot get: Shopify's own card readers, Tap to Pay, or in-person Shopify Payments rates.

# Barcode operations for a solo Shopify merchant — research report (2026-07-09)

## JOB A — one-time full-stock capture (garage walk-through)

### (a) Bluetooth scanner in HID keyboard mode → Google Sheets/Excel on Android
- This is the simplest working setup and is well documented: wireless/Bluetooth scanners pair as a **HID keyboard**, and virtually all of them can be configured (by scanning setup barcodes in the manual) to append an **Enter (CR) or Tab suffix** after each scan (source: tera-digital.com scanner guide). With an Enter suffix, each scan lands in a cell and the cursor drops to the next row — barcode column fills itself; the owner only needs to type quantities or scan the same code N times and aggregate later with a COUNTIF.
- Real-world confirmation on Android specifically: a merchant using a Bluetooth NETUM scanner into Google Sheets reported it "works perfectly on an android tablet" (the same setup was flaky on iPad — Android is the safer tablet choice here) (reddit r/googlesheets).
- **Offline**: the Google Sheets Android app supports offline editing when the spreadsheet is marked "Available offline" (Google's standard offline docs, support.google.com/docs/answer/6388102 — stable first-party doc, not re-fetched this session). Edits sync when connectivity returns — relevant since garages may have no Wi‑Fi. Caveat: mark the sheet offline BEFORE leaving coverage. Excel on Android also edits local files offline. One caution: a HID scanner is a "keyboard", so Android may hide the on-screen keyboard while it is connected — expect to toggle the soft keyboard to type quantities (widely reported behavior; not separately sourced).

### (b) Scanner MEMORY/BATCH mode (no live connection at all)
- Purpose-built for exactly this job: the scanner stores scans in internal flash while disconnected, then dumps them later. How it works on the two big brands:
  - **Zebra (DS4-series etc.)**: scan an "Enter Batch Mode" config barcode → all reads are stored; later scan "Send Batch Data" and the scanner transmits the whole buffer to the host (docs.zebra.com DS4678 programming guide).
  - **Honeywell Gen-6**: offers **Automatic Batch Mode** — the scanner stores data whenever it's out of radio range and auto-transmits when back in range of its base (sps-support.honeywell.com).
  - Budget brands (NETUM, Tera, Eyoyo, ScanAvenger, Inateck…) call it "Storage mode": data saved locally offline, uploaded later — typically by reconnecting via BT/USB and scanning an "upload data" barcode, at which point the scanner **replays all stored codes as keystrokes** into whatever app has focus (e.g., a Google Sheet column). Sources: tera-digital.com wireless-scanner guide ("Storage Mode saves data locally when offline and uploads it later"); ScanAvenger storage-mode tutorial (YouTube).
- **Capacity**: batch scanners "typically have sufficient internal memory to store a large volume of barcode scans" (free-barcode.com overview). Budget models commonly advertise tens of thousands to 100,000+ codes on their internal flash, but exact per-model figures were not verified in this research — check the specific model's spec sheet before buying (marked unknown rather than guessed).
- Practical note for Job A: memory mode stores barcode strings only (usually with timestamp on some models) — quantities still have to be captured either by scanning an item once per unit or by editing the sheet afterwards.

### (c) Camera-based apps (zero-hardware fallback)
- **Orca Scan** (iOS/Android, syncs scans to a cloud sheet, exportable): **Free plan = 1 user, 50 rows per sheet, $0** (orcascan.com/pricing) — too small for a multi-hundred-SKU garage capture without paying. Paid: Starter $20/mo, and the **Google Sheets live integration is gated to the Business plan at $40/mo (~€37)** (barcodesender.com comparison). Verdict: fine for a quick trial, not for the full capture on free tier.
- **Scandit**: enterprise scanning SDK aimed at developers/fleets, sold via sales contact with trial — no merchant-friendly free tier confirmed; limits **unknown** (not verified within call budget — do not rely on it for this use case).
- **CLZ Barry**: known as a free "barcode scanner as wireless keyboard" companion app that beams camera scans to a computer, i.e. could type into a desktop Google Sheet; its current status/limits were **not verified** this session — treat as unverified until checked at clz.com/barry.
- Overall: camera apps are slower and more battery-hungry than a €30–60 Bluetooth HID scanner for hundreds of scans; HID scanner + Android tablet + offline Google Sheet is the recommended Job A rig, with memory mode as the fallback if pairing is unreliable in the garages.

## JOB B — ongoing Shopify barcode operations

### Assigning barcodes to products/variants
- Every Shopify variant has a native **"Barcode (ISBN, UPC, GTIN, etc.)" field**, editable per-variant, via the admin **bulk editor** (add the Barcode column, paste values), or via **product CSV import** ("Variant Barcode" column) — standard Shopify product docs (help.shopify.com/en/manual/products — stable first-party docs; URLs not individually fetched this session, see notes). The Job A spreadsheet (barcode + qty) maps directly onto a CSV import or a Matrixify-style bulk update.

### Scan-driven apps (all pricing USD/month as listed on the Shopify App Store)
- **EasyScan (listing: "506 EasyScan SKU & Barcode", apps.shopify.com/easyscan-inventory-and-order)** — barcode/SKU assignment, label printing, scan-based stocktakes and inventory updates, order checking. **Basic $9.99/mo (or $99.90/yr)** including unlimited barcode generation + label printing; higher tiers add inventory check/update/transfer and order fulfilment — top tier $39.99/mo (developer site 506.io shows Basic 9.99 / Standard 39.99; a 2024–25 review lists 9.99/24.99/39.99 — mid-tier price conflicting, verify in-store). Marketed as a Stocky replacement. Best single-app fit for "assign internal barcodes + stocktake + print labels" on one cheap plan.
- **StockSavvy Barcode Scanning (apps.shopify.com/stock-savvy)** — scan-based cycle counts / stocktakes with discrepancy reports, purchase orders, label printing. Entry tier **$9/mo: 500 SKUs per count, unlimited counts, 20 POs/mo, unlimited barcode label printing** (App Store listing snippet); higher tiers exist but were not enumerated.
- **Stocky (first-party, POS Pro)** — **do not adopt: it is being sunset.** No new installs since Feb 2, 2026, and the app **stops working entirely after August 31, 2026**; Shopify tells merchants to move to the built-in "Inventory management" features (help.shopify.com Stocky page; inflowinventory.com and pimsical.app migration explainers; community.shopify.com thread). Historically it was bundled free with POS Pro — now irrelevant for new setups.
- **iPacky (apps.shopify.com/ipacky)** — pick/pack/fulfil with barcode verification of every item, picking lists, bin locations, bundles, shipping connectors. **Free "Starter" plan up to 50 shop orders/month**; Standard $19.99/mo + per-order metering ($0.099 first 500 orders, decreasing); 14-day trial; runs in the browser on any device incl. Android; 5.0★ (126 reviews). For a solo merchant with low order volume the free plan may be enough.
- **"Pikr" — no app by this name could be found on the Shopify App Store** (site-scoped search returned nothing). The closest match the searches surfaced is **"Order Picking App" (apps.shopify.com/order-picking-app)**: $14.95/mo (≤10 orders/day), $24.95/mo (≤20/day), $69.95/mo, with ~17% annual discounts. Treat "Pikr" as either renamed, delisted, or misremembered — verify with the client.

### Retail Barcode Labels (free, first-party) + printers
- **Retail Barcode Labels** (help.shopify.com/en/manual/sell-in-person/hardware/barcode-printer/retail-barcode-labels) is Shopify's free app to design label templates and **print barcode labels from within Shopify admin**; per Shopify docs it also covers creating barcodes for products that lack them (auto-generated internal barcodes assigned to the variant barcode field). It requires a **supported label printer**, and printing runs through the **desktop admin + printer's desktop software** — this is not an Android printing flow.
- **Officially supported printers (help.shopify.com barcode-printer page, with regional availability)**: Brother QL-1110NWB (Canada/US/Australia); DYMO LabelWriter 550 (Canada/US listed — DYMO software, Mac 10.14+/Win 8.1+); Zebra ZD220 (Canada/US/Ireland/UK — can't print from iOS or directly through a browser); **Zebra ZD420/ZD421 (Canada/US + various EU countries — the main officially-EU-supported option)**; Bixolon XD5-40dK/BEG (UK). Note for a Malta/EU merchant: the Zebra ZD421 line is the safest "officially supported" pick; DYMO 550 works technically anywhere but Shopify only lists CA/US support.
- **EU street prices (Galaxus.be toplist, EUR, 2026)**: DYMO LabelWriter 550 **€98.77** / 550 Turbo €175.39 (USB, desktop-only — no Android); Brother QL-600B €79.15 / QL-800 **€110.44** (USB, desktop); Zebra ZD220 **€193.34** (USB; ZD421 costs more, price not captured); NIIMBOT B1 **€50.31**, B21 **€65.90**, B21 Pro €63.90 (Bluetooth — print from the NIIMBOT Android/iOS app, but NOT integrated with Shopify's Retail Barcode Labels; fine for ad-hoc internal labels driven from a spreadsheet/app). Phomemo/Nelko EUR prices: not captured — unknown (same class as NIIMBOT, Bluetooth + Android app, no Shopify integration).
- **Android printing summary**: cheap BT label makers (NIIMBOT/Phomemo/Nelko) print from their own Android apps only; the Shopify-supported Zebra/DYMO/Brother desktop thermal printers print via desktop. If the client wants scan→print on Android inside Shopify, that's an app feature (e.g., EasyScan label printing) rather than Retail Barcode Labels.

## Recommended combo (solo merchant, Malta)
Job A: €30–60 Bluetooth 1D/2D scanner with HID + Enter suffix + memory mode as backup, Android tablet, offline-enabled Google Sheet. Job B: import barcodes via CSV/bulk editor; EasyScan Basic ($9.99) for barcode assignment + labels + stocktakes (or StockSavvy $9 if PO-driven counts matter); iPacky free tier for pick/pack; skip Stocky (sunset Aug 2026); labels via Retail Barcode Labels + Zebra ZD421 if official support matters, or a €50–66 NIIMBOT for pragmatic internal labels.

scanners.notes: LOAD-BEARING SHOPIFY ANSWER (from current official docs, scraped 2026-07-09): A Socket Mobile is NOT required. Shopify's supported-scanner page now lists Socket Mobile 1D/2D, Zebra DS2208, Zebra DS2278, AND 'Any HID (Human Interface Device) barcode scanner' (https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/sell-in-person/hardware/barcode-scanners). The dedicated HID page states 'You can use most HID scanners with Shopify POS' and documents the flow for generic scanners: pair via the device's system Bluetooth settings, then enable the 'Allow HID mode' toggle in POS Settings; scanning then adds products to cart from the home screen and works for product/order/customer search (https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/sell-in-person/hardware/barcode-scanners/hid-scanners). Android requirement: Android 10+ with Google Play/Mobile Services (https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/sell-in-person/hardware/barcode-scanners/requirements). PRACTICAL HID QUIRKS (all from the same docs): (1) while an HID scanner is connected Android hides the on-screen keyboard - fix via Settings > Physical keyboard > 'Show on-screen keyboard'; (2) scanning a variant barcode surfaces the master product and the variant must be tapped manually; (3) scanners cannot add products to inventory inside the POS app - stock-capture/inventory counts go through the Stocky app WITH an HID scanner (this actually favors a generic HID gun over Socket app-mode for use-case (a)); (4) HID is one-code-at-a-time, flagged by Shopify as 'might not be suitable for high-volume scanning'. Older community threads claiming Socket-only compatibility (e.g. community.shopify.com/t/140786) predate the current docs and are OBSOLETE, though a 2023-era thread confirms only HID-keyboard mode (not SPP/serial) works for generic scanners (https://community.shopify.com/t/new-bluetooth-scanner-barcode-not-recognized/568524). Socket app-mode remains the smoothest UX (no keyboard suppression, in-app battery status) but costs ~EUR 307 in the EU - over budget.
